name: Easter Island (Rapa Nui), Chile
clues: Hundreds of stone giants with heads but no feet, / most turn their backs where the ocean waves beat.
My statues are called moai, and I'm a lone island far out in the South Pacific, owned by a South American country. What am I?
Giant carved heads called moai. Part of Chile, deep in the Pacific.
fact: Most moai face inland, watching over the villages that carved them.

name: Hermitage Museum, St Petersburg, Russia
clues: Mint-green walls and a million gold frames, / with cats in the cellar, each with their own names.
I'm a winter palace turned art museum on the Neva River, in the city Peter the Great built. What am I?
A giant art museum on the Neva River.
fact: The Hermitage was founded by Catherine the Great in 1764.

name: Taipei 101, Taiwan
clues: Stacked up like bamboo, in eight-floor parts, / I sway with a giant gold ball at my heart.
My name is a number, and I'm the tallest tower in an island capital off southeast China. What am I?
A skyscraper in Taiwan's capital.
fact: Taipei 101 was the tallest building in the world from 2004 to 2010.

name: Plitvice Lakes, Croatia
clues: Sixteen blue lakes on a staircase of trees, / with boardwalks above them and falls in the breeze.
I'm a national park of terraced lakes and waterfalls in the Balkans, inland from the Adriatic. What am I?
A national park of terraced lakes in Croatia.
fact: The lakes are separated by natural dams of travertine that are still growing.

name: Okavango Delta, Botswana
clues: A river that dies in the desert, not sea, / and spreads into islands where elephants roam free.
Every winter my floods arrive from Angola and turn the Kalahari green, in a country next to South Africa. What am I?
A giant inland delta in Botswana.
fact: The Okavango floods at the height of the dry season, because the rain falls months earlier in Angola.

name: Matterhorn, Switzerland and Italy
clues: A crooked stone tooth that bites into the sky, / above a town where no gas cars drive by.
I'm the pyramid peak above Zermatt, on the Swiss and Italian border, and I'm on a famous chocolate box. What am I?
A pyramid-shaped peak above Zermatt.
fact: The Matterhorn was first climbed in 1865 by Edward Whymper's team.

name: Meteora, Greece
clues: Monasteries perched on tall pillars of rock, / once reached by a rope and a basket, not a walk.
My name means suspended in the air, and I'm on a plain in central Greece. What am I?
Monasteries on top of rock pillars in central Greece.
fact: Six of Meteora's monasteries are still active today.

name: Chichen Itza, Mexico
clues: Four staircases climb to a temple up high, / where a snake made of shadow slides down the sky.
On the spring equinox crowds watch a serpent of light on my pyramid, in Mexico's Yucatán. What am I?
The great Maya pyramid of El Castillo in the Yucatán.
fact: El Castillo has 91 steps on each of its four sides, plus the top platform, for 365 in all.

name: Antelope Canyon, Arizona, USA
clues: A crack in the sandstone, all ribbons and waves, / where sunbeams fall down like spotlights in caves.
I'm a narrow slot canyon on Navajo land near Page, Arizona, famous for photos of light beams. What am I?
A narrow slot canyon near Page, Arizona, on Navajo land.
fact: Antelope Canyon is only a few meters wide in places, and flash floods still carve it after storms.

name: Charles Bridge, Prague, Czechia
clues: Thirty dark saints line my cobblestone way, / where painters and buskers play night and day.
I'm a 14th-century stone bridge over the Vltava, between a castle and an old town square. What am I?
A medieval stone bridge over the Vltava River.
fact: Construction of Charles Bridge began in 1357.

name: Cliffs of Moher, Ireland
clues: Two hundred meters of cliff wall fall sheer, / into the Atlantic, where puffins live near.
I'm a line of sea cliffs on Ireland's west coast, in County Clare. What am I?
Famous sea cliffs in County Clare, Ireland.
fact: The Cliffs of Moher stretch for about 14 km.

name: Giant's Causeway, Northern Ireland
clues: Forty thousand stone columns with six tidy sides, / like stepping stones laid for a giant's long strides.
Legend says Finn McCool built me to cross to Scotland, on the north coast of Northern Ireland. What am I?
Basalt columns on the coast of County Antrim.
fact: The columns formed about 60 million years ago when lava cooled and cracked.

name: Perito Moreno Glacier, Argentina
clues: A blue wall of ice that's as tall as a block, / it groans and it cracks, then it falls with a shock.
I'm a glacier you can watch from boardwalks near El Calafate, in Argentine Patagonia. What am I?
A giant glacier in Los Glaciares National Park, in Argentine Patagonia.
fact: Perito Moreno's ice wall rises about 70 m above the lake, and chunks crash off it all day.

name: Pinnacles Desert, Australia
clues: Thousands of stone fingers point up from the sand, / in yellow dunes near a coast, in a dry, sunny land.
I'm a desert of limestone spires a couple of hours north of Perth, in Western Australia. What am I?
Limestone spires in Nambung National Park, north of Perth.
fact: There are thousands of pinnacles, some up to 3.5 m tall.

name: Iguazu Falls, Argentina and Brazil
clues: Two hundred and seventy falls in a row, / with a Devil's Throat roaring and rainbows below.
I'm a giant horseshoe of waterfalls on the border of Argentina and Brazil. What am I?
Giant waterfalls on the Argentina and Brazil border.
fact: Iguazu is made of about 275 separate waterfalls spread over nearly 3 km.

name: Milford Sound, New Zealand
clues: A pointed green peak rising out of the sea, / with waterfalls pouring as rain falls on me.
I'm a fjord with Mitre Peak, at the end of a long road on New Zealand's South Island. What am I?
A deep fjord in the far southwest of New Zealand's South Island.
fact: Milford Sound gets about 6.8 m of rain a year, making it one of the wettest places on Earth.

name: Golden Temple, Amritsar, India
clues: A temple of gold in a pool still and bright, / its kitchen feeds thousands each day and each night.
I'm the holiest place of the Sikhs, in Amritsar, near India's border with Pakistan. What am I?
The holiest shrine of Sikhism, covered in gold.
fact: Anyone can eat at the Golden Temple's langar, whatever their religion.

name: Serengeti, Tanzania
clues: A million gnu thunder across golden grass, / and crocodiles wait where the river herds pass.
My name means endless plains, and my great migration crosses into Kenya's Maasai Mara. What am I?
A famous savanna national park in Tanzania.
fact: The great migration includes about 1.5 million wildebeest plus hundreds of thousands of zebras.

name: Twelve Apostles, Australia
clues: Tall stacks of limestone stand out in the waves, / fewer each year, as the sea digs their graves.
We're named after twelve, but there were never that many, beside the Great Ocean Road in Victoria, Australia. What are we?
Limestone stacks along the Great Ocean Road.
fact: The cliffs here retreat about 2 cm a year.

name: Monument Valley, USA
clues: Red stone towers rise out of the plain, / where cowboys rode in films again and again.
I'm a valley of giant red buttes in the Navajo Nation, on the Arizona and Utah border. What am I?
Red sandstone buttes on the Arizona and Utah border, in the Navajo Nation.
fact: Monument Valley has been the backdrop of dozens of Western films since the 1930s.

name: Pamukkale, Turkey
clues: White terraces shine like a hillside of snow, / with warm turquoise pools where barefoot people go.
My name means cotton castle, and I sit next to the ruins of Hierapolis in western Türkiye. What am I?
Pamukkale, in southwestern Turkey.
fact: Visitors to Pamukkale must walk the terraces barefoot to protect the soft travertine.

name: Uluru, Australia
clues: A red rock alone in a sea of red sand, / it glows orange at sunset, the heart of the land.
I'm a giant sandstone monolith sacred to the Anangu people, in Australia's Northern Territory. What am I?
Uluru, also called Ayers Rock.
fact: Uluru is about 348 m high and 9.4 km around at its base.

name: Bran Castle, Romania
clues: A castle of towers on a rock, white and tall, / where Dracula fans come to see every hall.
I'm sold to tourists as Dracula's castle, on a mountain pass in Transylvania, Romania. What am I?
A castle in the Carpathians near Brașov.
fact: Bram Stoker never visited Romania.

name: Guanajuato, Mexico
clues: Houses in candy colors climb up a ravine, / with tunnels below where the old rivers had been.
I'm a colonial silver-mining city in central Mexico, famous for its narrow Alley of the Kiss. What am I?
A colorful colonial city of tunnels and alleys in central Mexico.
fact: Guanajuato's streets run partly through old tunnels, first built to control floods.

name: Naqsh-e Jahan Square, Isfahan, Iran
clues: A long royal square with blue mosques at each side, / and a palace and bazaar where merchants once cried.
My city was once called half the world, and I'm its great square, in central Iran. What am I?
The great square of Isfahan, Iran, lined with blue-tiled mosques.
fact: It's one of the largest city squares in the world, about 560 m long.

name: Banaue Rice Terraces, Philippines
clues: Green stairs of rice climbing high up the slopes, / carved long ago with stone tools and with ropes.
I'm ancient rice terraces carved by the Ifugao people, in the mountains of Luzon, Philippines. What am I?
Ancient rice terraces in the mountains of northern Luzon, Philippines.
fact: The Ifugao people carved these terraces by hand about 2,000 years ago.

name: Grand Palace, Bangkok, Thailand
clues: Gold spires and guardians with fierce painted faces, / and a little green Buddha in a temple of graces.
I'm the old royal palace by the Chao Phraya River, home of the Emerald Buddha, in Bangkok. What am I?
The royal palace of Bangkok, home of the Emerald Buddha.
fact: The Grand Palace was home to Thailand's kings from 1782.

name: Space Needle, Seattle, USA
clues: A saucer on legs that looks out from the sky, / built for a fair when space dreams were high.
I'm a futuristic tower in a rainy city of the Pacific Northwest, USA. What am I?
The flying-saucer tower of Seattle, Washington.
fact: The Space Needle was built for the 1962 World's Fair and is 184 m tall.

name: Kīlauea, Hawaii, USA
clues: I bleed glowing lava that hisses at sea, / and a goddess named Pele is said to live in me.
I'm one of the most active volcanoes on Earth, on Hawaii's Big Island. What am I?
A volcano on Hawaii's Big Island.
fact: Kīlauea erupted almost continuously from 1983 to 2018.

name: French Quarter, New Orleans, USA
clues: Iron lace balconies, jazz on the street, / with beignets and beads and a brass band beat.
I'm the oldest neighborhood of a city on the Mississippi, famous for Mardi Gras. What am I?
The old French Quarter of New Orleans, Louisiana.
fact: The French Quarter is the oldest neighborhood in New Orleans, laid out in 1718.

name: Great Blue Hole, Belize
clues: A circle of navy in a turquoise sea, / a sinkhole so deep that the sharks swim in me.
I'm a giant round sinkhole on a reef off the coast of Belize, in the Caribbean. What am I?
The Great Blue Hole, off the coast of Belize.
fact: The Great Blue Hole is about 300 m across and 125 m deep.

name: Château Frontenac, Quebec City, Canada
clues: A green-roofed castle that's really a hotel, / on a cliff above a river where old cannons dwell.
I tower over the walled old town of the capital of Canada's French-speaking province. What am I?
The castle-like hotel above the St Lawrence River in Quebec City.
fact: The Château Frontenac opened in 1893 and is often called the most photographed hotel in the world.

name: Mont-Saint-Michel, France
clues: An abbey on a rock where the tide races in, / twice a day it's an island, and then it's not again.
I'm a tidal island topped with an abbey, where Normandy meets Brittany, in France. What am I?
A tidal island abbey off the coast of Normandy.
fact: The tides around Mont-Saint-Michel are among the strongest in Europe, up to 14 m.

name: Zhangjiajie, China
clues: Stone towers like fingers rise up through the mist, / they inspired a blue-alien film that you might have missed.
I'm a forest of sandstone pillars with a glass bridge, in Hunan province, China. What am I?
A forest park of stone towers in Hunan.
fact: One pillar was renamed 'Avatar Hallelujah Mountain' in 2010.

name: Old Faithful, Yellowstone, USA
clues: A hot fountain of steam that erupts on the hour, / or near it, so rangers can guess its next shower.
I'm the most famous geyser in the world's first national park, in Wyoming, USA. What am I?
The famous geyser in the world's first national park.
fact: Old Faithful erupts roughly every 60 to 110 minutes.

name: Terracotta Army, Xi'an, China
clues: Eight thousand clay soldiers, each face is unique, / they guard an old emperor's tomb, so to speak.
Farmers digging a well found us near Xi'an, the old capital of China. What are we?
Clay warriors guarding China's first emperor.
fact: About 8,000 soldiers, 130 chariots and 670 horses are thought to be buried there.

name: Varanasi, India
clues: Stone steps to a river where fires burn bright, / and pilgrims float flowers and candles at night.
I'm one of the oldest living cities, on the Ganges in Uttar Pradesh, India. What am I?
One of the oldest living cities, on the Ganges.
fact: Varanasi has more than 80 ghats along the Ganges.

name: Sossusvlei, Namibia
clues: Red dunes so tall they could hide a skyscraper, / and dead black trees on a white clay paper.
I'm a valley of giant red dunes with Deadvlei nearby, in the Namib Desert of Namibia. What am I?
Red sand dunes in the Namib Desert.
fact: The Namib is often called the oldest desert in the world, at around 55 million years.

name: Bagan, Myanmar
clues: Two thousand brick temples spread over a plain, / with balloons drifting over at dawn once again.
I'm an ancient temple city on the Irrawaddy River in Myanmar. What am I?
An ancient temple city on the Irrawaddy River in Myanmar.
fact: Over 10,000 temples were built at Bagan between the 11th and 13th centuries.

name: Sugarloaf Mountain, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
clues: A cable car climbs to a granite dome's top, / where beaches and a bay make your jaw drop.
I'm a rounded granite peak at the mouth of Guanabara Bay, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. What am I?
The granite peak with a cable car at the mouth of Guanabara Bay, Rio de Janeiro.
fact: Sugarloaf's cable car first opened in 1912.

name: Valparaíso, Chile
clues: Steep hills of bright houses with murals so wide, / and old wooden elevators to take you for a ride.
I'm a colorful port city on Chile's Pacific coast, an hour or two from Santiago. What am I?
The colorful hillside port city on Chile's Pacific coast.
fact: Valparaíso's old funicular elevators have been carrying people up its hills since the 1880s.

name: Hassan II Mosque, Casablanca, Morocco
clues: A minaret taller than most towers you've seen, / and a mosque half on the ocean, tiled in green.
I'm a giant mosque built partly over the Atlantic, in Morocco's biggest city. What am I?
A huge seaside mosque in Casablanca, Morocco.
fact: Its minaret is about 210 m tall, one of the tallest in the world.

name: Kruger National Park, South Africa
clues: The Big Five all roam in my bushland so wide, / from the Crocodile River to the Limpopo side.
I'm South Africa's biggest safari park, along the border with Mozambique. What am I?
South Africa's biggest safari park, on the border with Mozambique.
fact: Kruger is home to all of the Big Five: lion, leopard, elephant, rhino and buffalo.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro, Tanzania
clues: Snow on my crown, though the equator is near, / the tallest in Africa, I stand alone here.
I'm Africa's highest mountain, a lone volcano in Tanzania near the Kenya border. What am I?
Africa's highest peak, in Tanzania.
fact: Kilimanjaro's summit, Uhuru Peak, is 5,895 m above sea level.

name: Cinque Terre, Italy
clues: Five colorful villages clinging to cliffs, / linked by a train and by paths, and by skiffs.
I'm a string of five cliffside fishing villages on the Italian Riviera, near La Spezia. What am I?
Five colorful cliff villages on the Italian Riviera.
fact: The five villages are linked by footpaths and a train, and cars are mostly kept out.

name: Wadi Rum, Jordan
clues: Red sand and tall cliffs where the Bedouins camp, / it played planet Mars with a camera and lamp.
I'm a red desert valley in southern Jordan, where Lawrence of Arabia rode. What am I?
The Valley of the Moon desert in southern Jordan.
fact: Wadi Rum has stood in for Mars in films like The Martian.

name: Rainbow Mountain (Vinicunca), Peru
clues: Stripes of red, yellow and turquoise and gold, / on a mountain so high that the air's thin and cold.
I'm a rainbow-striped mountain about 5,000 m high, a day trip from Cusco, Peru. What am I?
A striped mountain in the Andes, a day trip from Cusco, Peru.
fact: Vinicunca's top is about 5,200 m high, and its stripes are layers of different minerals.

name: Chocolate Hills, Bohol, Philippines
clues: A thousand round hills like gumdrops in a row, / that turn chocolate-brown when the dry months go.
I'm a field of cone-shaped hills named after a sweet treat, on the island of Bohol, Philippines. What am I?
Cone-shaped hills on Bohol island.
fact: There are at least 1,260 Chocolate Hills.

name: Lake Baikal, Russia
clues: The deepest of lakes, so clear you see down, / and seals live inside me, far from any town.
I'm the world's deepest and oldest lake, in southern Siberia, Russia. What am I?
Lake Baikal.
fact: Lake Baikal is about 25 million years old and more than 1,600 m deep.

name: Nazca Lines, Peru
clues: A hummingbird, monkey and spider in sand, / so big you must fly to see what's been planned.
I'm a set of giant ancient drawings on the desert floor of southern Peru. What am I?
Giant desert drawings in southern Peru.
fact: The lines have survived so long because the area gets almost no rain or wind.

name: Petra, Jordan
clues: A treasury carved from a cliff of pink stone, / at the end of a canyon, an ancient city's own.
I'm the rose-red city of the Nabataeans, reached through a narrow gorge in southern Jordan. What am I?
The ancient Nabataean city of Petra.
fact: Scientists estimate that around 85% of Petra is still buried and unexcavated.

name: Plaza de España, Seville, Spain
clues: A half-circle palace with bridges and tiles, / each province of Spain has an alcove for miles.
I'm a grand plaza with a canal, built for a 1929 fair, in the capital of Andalusia. What am I?
A grand half-circle plaza in Seville, in southern Spain.
fact: The plaza was built for the 1929 Ibero-American Exposition.

name: Mount Bromo, Indonesia
clues: A smoking gray crater in a sea made of sand, / at sunrise the climbers look down where they stand.
I'm an active volcano inside a giant caldera in East Java, Indonesia. What am I?
An active volcano in East Java.
fact: The Tenggerese people hold the Yadnya Kasada festival at Bromo every year.

name: Bora Bora, French Polynesia
clues: A green jagged peak in a ring of lagoon, / with huts over water beneath the full moon.
I'm an island famous for overwater bungalows, northwest of Tahiti, in French Polynesia. What am I?
An island in French Polynesia.
fact: Overwater bungalows were invented in French Polynesia in the 1960s.

name: Li River at Xingping, Guilin, China
clues: Green peaks like dragon teeth line a calm stream, / where fishermen float on bamboo rafts in a dream.
My karst peaks are on the back of China's 20-yuan note, near Guilin, in southern China. What am I?
Karst peaks along the Li River near Guilin, in southern China.
fact: This view of the Li River is printed on the back of China's 20-yuan note.

name: Victoria Peak, Hong Kong
clues: A tram climbs so steep that the buildings all lean, / to a view of a harbor with skyscrapers between.
I'm the highest hill on Hong Kong Island, looking over Victoria Harbour. What am I?
The highest hill on Hong Kong Island.
fact: Hong Kong has more skyscrapers than any other city in the world.

name: Rock of Gibraltar
clues: A limestone lion that guards the sea's gate, / where monkeys will snatch any snack that you ate.
I'm a British rock at the southern tip of Spain, facing Morocco across the strait. What am I?
A British limestone rock at the tip of Spain.
fact: About 300 Barbary macaques live on the Rock of Gibraltar.

name: Bay of Kotor, Montenegro
clues: A fjord in the south where the mountains meet sea, / with a walled old town and steep walls up to me.
I'm a winding bay with a medieval walled town, on the Adriatic coast of Montenegro. What am I?
A fjord-like bay with a walled old town in Montenegro.
fact: Kotor's town walls climb about 1,350 steps up the mountain behind it.

name: Hoi An, Vietnam
clues: Silk lanterns glowing on yellow old walls, / with tailors and boats and a bridge built with halls.
I'm an old trading port of lanterns and tailors, near Da Nang, in central Vietnam. What am I?
An old lantern-lit trading town on the coast of central Vietnam.
fact: Hoi An's Japanese Covered Bridge dates from the 1590s.

name: Edinburgh Castle, Scotland
clues: A castle that sits on an old volcano's plug, / above a royal mile where the bagpipes tug.
I'm the castle above the capital of Scotland, where a gun fires at one o'clock. What am I?
The castle on the rock above Scotland's capital.
fact: The One O'Clock Gun has been fired since 1861 so ships could set their clocks.

name: Stari Most, Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina
clues: A white stone arch high over green water, / where divers leap down, each son and each daughter.
I'm an Ottoman stone bridge over the Neretva River, rebuilt after the war, in Bosnia and Herzegovina. What am I?
The old arched bridge of Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina.
fact: Stari Most was destroyed in 1993 and rebuilt with stones raised from the river.

name: Ngorongoro Crater, Tanzania
clues: A giant bowl made when a volcano fell in, / full of lions and rhinos and zebras within.
I'm a huge volcanic crater full of wildlife, near the Serengeti in northern Tanzania. What am I?
A giant volcanic crater full of wildlife in northern Tanzania.
fact: Ngorongoro is the largest unbroken, unflooded volcanic caldera in the world, about 20 km across.

name: Gyeongbokgung Palace, Seoul, South Korea
clues: Wooden halls painted red, green and blue, / with guards in bright robes and a mountain view too.
I'm the main royal palace of the Joseon kings, in the heart of Seoul, South Korea. What am I?
The main royal palace of Seoul, South Korea.
fact: Gyeongbokgung was first built in 1395, and visitors wearing hanbok get in free.

name: Boulders Beach, Cape Town, South Africa
clues: Penguins waddle on sand between giant gray stones, / in Africa, of all places, they've made their homes.
I'm a beach full of African penguins near Simon's Town, south of Cape Town. What am I?
The penguin beach near Simon's Town, Cape Town.
fact: A colony of a few thousand African penguins lives on Boulders Beach.

name: Caminito, La Boca, Buenos Aires
clues: Tin houses painted in red, blue and green, / where tango dancers swirl on the street scene.
I'm a colorful street in the old port district of La Boca, in Buenos Aires, Argentina. What am I?
The colorful street of La Boca in Buenos Aires, Argentina.
fact: La Boca's tin houses were painted with leftover ship paint, which is why they're so colorful.

name: Brandenburg Gate, Berlin, Germany
clues: A chariot with four horses on top of my gate, / where a wall cut a city, and made it wait.
I'm a famous gate in the center of Berlin, Germany. What am I?
The famous gate in the heart of Berlin.
fact: The Berlin Wall ran right beside the Brandenburg Gate from 1961 to 1989.

name: Valley of the Kings, Luxor, Egypt
clues: A desert valley where pharaohs were laid, / in painted tombs with their gold and their jade.
I'm the burial valley of the pharaohs on the West Bank of the Nile, across from Luxor, Egypt. What am I?
The royal tombs across the Nile from Luxor, Egypt.
fact: Tutankhamun's tomb was found here almost untouched in 1922.

name: Angkor Wat, Cambodia
clues: Five lotus towers that rise from a moat, / the largest of temples, and jungle afloat.
I'm the great temple near Siem Reap, and I'm on the flag of Cambodia. What am I?
Angkor Wat temple in Cambodia.
fact: Angkor Wat faces west, which is unusual for a temple of its kind, and the sun rises right behind its towers at the equinox.

name: Dead Sea
clues: You float like a cork and you can't really sink, / it's the lowest place on land, and too salty to drink.
I'm a salt lake on Jordan's western border, more than 400 m below sea level. What am I?
A lake so salty it is called 'dead'.
fact: The Dead Sea's shore is about 430 m below sea level and the water level drops about 1 m a year.

name: Hampi, India
clues: Huge boulders are balanced like toys on the plain, / with a stone chariot where great kings used to reign.
I'm the ruins of the Vijayanagara empire's capital, in Karnataka, southern India. What am I?
The ruins of the Vijayanagara capital in Karnataka.
fact: Hampi's stone chariot at the Vittala Temple appears on India's 50-rupee note.

name: Kirkjufell, Iceland
clues: A cone of green mountain beside a calm bay, / with three little waterfalls posing all day.
I'm the most photographed mountain in Iceland, on the Snæfellsnes peninsula. What am I?
A cone-shaped mountain on Iceland's Snæfellsnes peninsula.
fact: Kirkjufell means 'church mountain'.

name: Badwater Basin, Death Valley, USA
clues: White salt in hexagons, baked in the heat, / the lowest of lows, under scorching sun's beat.
I'm a salt flat in Death Valley, California, the lowest point in North America. What am I?
A salt flat in Death Valley, California.
fact: Mount Whitney, the highest point in the lower 48 states, is less than 140 km from Badwater.

name: Tiger's Nest Monastery, Bhutan
clues: A monastery clinging to a sheer cliff face, / where legend says a tiger flew to this place.
I'm a cliffside monastery above the Paro Valley, in the Himalayan kingdom of Bhutan. What am I?
Paro Taktsang, a monastery in Bhutan.
fact: Bhutan measures its progress with Gross National Happiness.

name: Victoria Falls, Zambia and Zimbabwe
clues: A mile-wide curtain of thundering spray, / its mist looks like smoke from twenty miles away.
Locals call me the smoke that thunders, on the Zambezi between Zambia and Zimbabwe. What am I?
Victoria Falls on the Zambezi River.
fact: At full flood, more than 500 million liters of water per minute pour over Victoria Falls.

name: Lalibela, Ethiopia
clues: Churches carved down into red volcanic stone, / one shaped like a cross, standing deep and alone.
I'm a town of rock-cut churches in the highlands of northern Ethiopia. What am I?
Rock-hewn churches in the Ethiopian highlands.
fact: Lalibela's 11 churches were carved around the 12th and 13th centuries and are still used for worship.

name: CN Tower, Toronto, Canada
clues: A needle of concrete with a disc near its top, / walk on the glass floor, if you dare, don't stop.
I'm a 553 m tower on the shore of Lake Ontario, in Canada's biggest city. What am I?
The tall tower by Lake Ontario in Toronto, Canada.
fact: The CN Tower is 553 m tall and has a glass floor 342 m up.

name: Erg Chebbi, Merzouga, Morocco
clues: Orange sand mountains that glow at sunset, / where camels lead campers, no roads, not yet.
I'm the great Sahara dunes near Merzouga, in eastern Morocco near Algeria. What am I?
The great sand dunes of the Sahara near Merzouga, Morocco.
fact: Erg Chebbi's tallest dunes rise about 150 m above the desert floor.

name: Shibuya Crossing, Tokyo, Japan
clues: When the lights all turn red, thousands cross every way, / under giant TV screens, all night and all day.
I'm the busiest crossing on Earth, outside a station where a loyal dog statue waits, in Tokyo. What am I?
The world's busiest pedestrian crossing, in Tokyo.
fact: The dog Hachikō waited at Shibuya Station for his owner every day for nearly ten years.

name: Preikestolen, Norway
clues: A square stone platform hung over a fjord, / six hundred meters, don't look down, you'll be floored.
I'm a flat-topped cliff called the Pulpit Rock, near Stavanger in southwest Norway. What am I?
A cliff above the Lysefjord in Norway.
fact: About 300,000 people hike to Preikestolen each year.

name: Alhambra, Granada, Spain
clues: A red fortress palace with fountains and tile, / with snowy peaks watching it all the while.
I'm a Moorish palace on a hill above Granada, below the Sierra Nevada, in Spain. What am I?
A Moorish palace above Granada.
fact: The Alhambra was the last stronghold of Muslim rule in Spain, until 1492.

name: Torres del Paine, Chile
clues: Three granite horns over lakes of bright blue, / where wind and guanacos and glaciers greet you.
I'm a national park of granite towers in Patagonia, in southern Chile. What am I?
A national park in Chilean Patagonia.
fact: 'Paine' is thought to mean 'blue' in the local Tehuelche language.

name: Registan, Samarkand, Uzbekistan
clues: Three schools with blue domes face one sandy square, / on the old Silk Road, with gold patterns there.
I'm a grand square of tiled madrasas in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. What am I?
The famous square of Samarkand.
fact: Registan means 'sandy place' in Persian.

name: Komodo Island, Indonesia
clues: Here dragons are real, with a venomous bite, / they're three meters long, but they don't take flight.
I'm an island in Indonesia's Lesser Sunda chain, home of the biggest lizards on Earth. What am I?
An island in the Lesser Sunda chain, home of dragons.
fact: Komodo dragons can grow to 3 m long.

name: Tikal, Guatemala
clues: Tall temple-tops poke through a jungle so green, / where howler monkeys roar and toucans are seen.
I'm a huge Maya city in the rainforest of northern Guatemala. What am I?
A great Maya city in the jungle of northern Guatemala.
fact: Tikal appeared as the Rebel base on Yavin 4 in the first Star Wars film in 1977.

name: Ilulissat Icefjord, Greenland
clues: Icebergs as tall as skyscrapers drift, / from the fastest of glaciers, they slowly shift.
I'm a fjord packed with icebergs on the west coast of Greenland. What am I?
An icefjord on Greenland's west coast.
fact: Sermeq Kujalleq glacier produces about 10% of Greenland's icebergs.

name: Etosha Pan, Namibia
clues: A white salty pan that's as flat as a plate, / where lions and zebras drink at waterholes late.
My name means great white place, and I'm a salt pan and safari park in northern Namibia. What am I?
A huge white salt pan and wildlife park in northern Namibia.
fact: Etosha means 'great white place' in the local Oshiwambo language.

name: Ushuaia, Argentina
clues: The end of the world, so the signs like to say, / where ships leave for the ice, far south, far away.
I'm the southernmost city, on Tierra del Fuego, where cruises leave for Antarctica, in Argentina. What am I?
The southernmost city on the island of Tierra del Fuego.
fact: Ushuaia was founded around a prison, which is now a museum.

name: Borobudur, Indonesia
clues: A hill wrapped in stone, with bells made of rock, / each one hides a Buddha, at dawn people flock.
I'm the largest Buddhist temple on Earth, near Yogyakarta on the island of Java, Indonesia. What am I?
The largest Buddhist temple in the world, on the island of Java.
fact: Borobudur was built in the 9th century from about two million stone blocks.

name: Havana, Cuba
clues: Old Chevys in pink drive along the sea wall, / with salsa and cigars and pastel houses tall.
I'm the capital of the biggest island in the Caribbean, famous for 1950s cars. What am I?
The capital of Cuba.
fact: Old Havana and its fortifications became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982.

name: Table Mountain, Cape Town, South Africa
clues: A mountain so flat a white cloud makes its cloth, / above a city near Africa's far southern growth.
I'm a flat-topped mountain with a rotating cable car above Cape Town, South Africa. What am I?
The flat-topped mountain above Cape Town.
fact: The constellation Mensa, 'the table', was named after Table Mountain in the 1750s.

name: Angel Falls, Venezuela
clues: The tallest of falls from a flat mountain top, / the water turns to mist before it can drop.
I'm the world's highest waterfall, falling off a tepui in the jungle of Venezuela. What am I?
The world's tallest waterfall, in Venezuela.
fact: Angel Falls drops 979 m, with an unbroken fall of 807 m.

name: Dubrovnik, Croatia
clues: Orange rooftops inside thick walls by the sea, / walk the ramparts, a fantasy show filmed me.
I'm a walled old town on the Adriatic, at the southern tip of Croatia. What am I?
A walled old town on the Adriatic coast.
fact: Dubrovnik's walls are nearly 2 km around and up to 25 m high.

name: Badshahi Mosque, Lahore, Pakistan
clues: Red sandstone walls and three white marble domes, / with a courtyard so big, a hundred thousand it homes.
I'm a great Mughal mosque in Lahore, in Pakistan's Punjab. What am I?
The great red sandstone mosque of Lahore, Pakistan.
fact: Finished in 1673, its courtyard can hold around 100,000 people.

name: Cartagena, Colombia
clues: Flowered balconies on yellow and pink, / inside old stone walls by the sea's warm brink.
I'm a walled colonial port on the Caribbean coast of Colombia. What am I?
A walled Caribbean port city in Colombia.
fact: Cartagena's city walls stretch about 11 km.

name: Lake Titicaca, Peru and Bolivia
clues: A lake in the clouds with floating reed isles, / where boats sail higher than anywhere for miles.
I'm the highest big navigable lake, on the border of Peru and Bolivia. What am I?
The highest navigable lake in the world, between Peru and Bolivia.
fact: Lake Titicaca sits about 3,812 m above sea level.

name: Chefchaouen, Morocco
clues: Every wall, every door, every step is blue, / in a mountain town where the cats wander through.
I'm the blue-painted town in the Rif Mountains of northern Morocco. What am I?
The blue city of northern Morocco.
fact: Chefchaouen was founded in 1471 as a small fortress.

name: Great Barrier Reef, Australia
clues: Coral gardens so big they're seen from space, / with turtles and clownfish in a warm, shallow place.
I'm the biggest coral reef system on Earth, off the coast of Queensland, Australia. What am I?
The giant coral reef off Queensland.
fact: The Great Barrier Reef is made of about 2,900 individual reefs.

name: Pompeii, Italy
clues: A Roman town frozen in ash on one day, / with bread in its ovens, and streets laid in gray.
I'm an ancient Roman town buried by Mount Vesuvius, near Naples, Italy. What am I?
A Roman town at the foot of Mount Vesuvius.
fact: Pompeii was rediscovered in the 1700s, about 1,600 years after it was buried.

name: Moraine Lake, Canada
clues: A lake of bright turquoise below jagged peaks, / it's frozen till June, for many long weeks.
I'm a glacier lake in the Valley of the Ten Peaks, in Banff National Park, Canada. What am I?
A glacier lake below ten peaks in Banff National Park.
fact: Moraine Lake is usually frozen until June.

name: Itsukushima Shrine, Miyajima, Japan
clues: A red gate that floats in the sea at high tide, / at low tide you walk out and stand by its side.
I'm a shrine with a floating torii gate on an island near Hiroshima, Japan. What am I?
The floating red torii gate of Miyajima, near Hiroshima.
fact: At high tide the great torii seems to float; at low tide you can walk out to it.

name: St Basil's Cathedral, Moscow, Russia
clues: Nine onion domes, swirled like candy and bright, / at the end of a square by red walls with a light.
I'm the colorful cathedral on Red Square, beside the Kremlin, in Moscow. What am I?
The colorful cathedral on Red Square.
fact: St Basil's was built in the 1550s to celebrate a military victory by Ivan the Terrible.

name: Nara Park, Japan
clues: Deer bow for crackers by temples of old, / and a giant bronze Buddha sits inside, I'm told.
I'm a park where a thousand deer roam freely, in Japan's first permanent capital, near Osaka. What am I?
The deer park around the temples of Nara, Japan.
fact: More than 1,000 deer roam Nara Park, and some have learned to bow for crackers.

name: Hawa Mahal, Jaipur, India
clues: A pink honeycomb wall of nine hundred small panes, / where royal ladies watched street parades and trains.
I'm the Palace of Winds in the Pink City of Jaipur, in Rajasthan, India. What am I?
The pink Palace of Winds in Jaipur, India.
fact: Hawa Mahal has 953 small windows, so royal women could watch the street without being seen.

name: Batu Caves, Malaysia
clues: Two hundred and seventy-two rainbow steps climb, / past a giant gold statue, to a cave for a time.
I'm a limestone cave temple with rainbow stairs and monkeys, just north of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. What am I?
Rainbow stairs and a golden statue at a limestone cave temple near Kuala Lumpur.
fact: The golden statue of Lord Murugan at Batu Caves is about 43 m tall.

name: White Temple (Wat Rong Khun), Chiang Rai, Thailand
clues: A temple all white with mirror-glass shine, / where hands reach up from a pit by the line.
I'm a dazzling all-white temple in Chiang Rai, in the far north of Thailand. What am I?
The all-white temple of Chiang Rai, in northern Thailand.
fact: The White Temple was designed by artist Chalermchai Kositpipat and opened in 1997.

name: Volcanoes National Park, Rwanda
clues: Misty green volcanoes where gentle giants roam, / silverback gorillas make bamboo their home.
I'm a national park of volcanoes and mountain gorillas, in the land of a thousand hills in central Africa. What am I?
Mountain gorilla forests on the Virunga volcanoes, in northwest Rwanda.
fact: Only about 1,000 mountain gorillas live in the wild, all in this corner of Africa.

name: Gateway of India, Mumbai, India
clues: A great stone arch facing out to the sea, / where a king and a queen once came to see me.
I'm a giant arch on the waterfront of India's biggest city, beside the Taj hotel. What am I?
The great arch on the waterfront of Mumbai.
fact: The Gateway of India was finished in 1924.

name: Lake Palace, Udaipur, India
clues: A white marble palace that floats on a lake, / in a city of lakes, for a royal's own sake.
I'm a palace hotel on Lake Pichola, in Udaipur, Rajasthan, India. What am I?
The white palace hotel on Lake Pichola, Udaipur.
fact: The Lake Palace covers almost its whole island, so it seems to float.

name: Avenue of the Baobabs, Madagascar
clues: Giant trees like they're planted with roots in the sky, / they line a red road as the sunset goes by.
I'm a dirt road lined with giant baobab trees near Morondava, on Madagascar's west coast. What am I?
A road of giant baobab trees near Morondava.
fact: Six of the world's eight baobab species grow only in Madagascar.

name: Tanah Lot, Bali, Indonesia
clues: A temple that sits on a rock in the waves, / at high tide it's an island, where the sea misbehaves.
I'm a Hindu sea temple on a rock off the coast of Bali, Indonesia. What am I?
A sea temple on a rock off the coast of Bali, Indonesia.
fact: At high tide, Tanah Lot's rock becomes a little island.

name: Nine Arch Bridge, Ella, Sri Lanka
clues: Nine stone arches carry a train through the tea, / in green misty hills, as pretty as can be.
I'm a stone railway bridge in the tea country near Ella, in Sri Lanka's hills. What am I?
A stone railway bridge among tea hills near Ella, Sri Lanka.
fact: The Nine Arch Bridge was built around 1921 without any steel.

name: Kuang Si Falls, Laos
clues: Milky blue pools in a jungle cascade, / where you swim down below in the cool forest shade.
I'm a turquoise waterfall near Luang Prabang, in landlocked Laos. What am I?
Turquoise waterfall pools near Luang Prabang, Laos.
fact: The water's milky blue color comes from limestone dissolved in it.

name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Abu Dhabi, UAE
clues: Eighty-two white domes and gold chandeliers, / with pools that reflect it, it shines like a mirror.
I'm a huge white marble mosque in the capital of the United Arab Emirates. What am I?
The great white mosque of Abu Dhabi.
fact: Its main prayer hall has one of the largest hand-knotted carpets in the world.

name: Jiuzhaigou, China
clues: Lakes blue as peacocks and waterfalls white, / with sunken old trees in the water so bright.
I'm a valley of colorful lakes in the mountains of Sichuan, China. What am I?
A valley of colorful lakes and waterfalls in Sichuan, China.
fact: Jiuzhaigou's lakes are so clear you can see fallen trees lying on the bottom.

name: Teotihuacan, Mexico
clues: An Avenue of the Dead leads to pyramids two, / the Sun and the Moon, and they're older than you knew.
I'm an ancient city of giant pyramids just northeast of Mexico City. What am I?
The Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, near Mexico City.
fact: At its peak around 500 AD, Teotihuacan may have had more than 100,000 people.

name: Galapagos Islands, Ecuador
clues: Giant tortoises plod and blue-footed birds dance, / where a young scientist found his big chance.
I'm a group of volcanic islands on the equator, 1,000 km off the coast of Ecuador. What am I?
The Galapagos Islands, part of Ecuador.
fact: Galapagos giant tortoises can live for more than 100 years.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle, Germany
clues: A fairy-tale castle on a hill in the Alps, / with white towers rising like sugar-glazed caps.
A dreamy king built me above a gorge in Bavaria, Germany, and a famous cartoon castle copied me. What am I?
A fairy-tale castle in the Bavarian Alps.
fact: King Ludwig II of Bavaria died in 1886, before Neuschwanstein was finished.

name: Atomium, Brussels, Belgium
clues: Nine shiny steel spheres linked up in a chain, / a giant iron crystal you can walk in, again.
I'm a giant model of an atom, built for the 1958 World's Fair in Brussels, Belgium. What am I?
Nine giant silver balls in Brussels.
fact: The Atomium is 102 m tall, and you can ride an escalator between its spheres.

name: Salar de Uyuni, Bolivia
clues: After the rain I become the world's mirror, / a white salt desert, nothing could be clearer.
I'm the biggest salt flat on Earth, high on the Altiplano of Bolivia. What am I?
The biggest salt flat in the world, high in the Andes of Bolivia.
fact: Salar de Uyuni covers more than 10,000 square kilometers and varies in height by less than a meter.

name: Shwedagon Pagoda, Yangon, Myanmar
clues: A great golden stupa that's covered in gems, / at dusk it glows bright, with diamond-tip hems.
I'm a giant golden pagoda on a hill in Yangon, the biggest city of Myanmar. What am I?
The giant golden stupa of Yangon, Myanmar.
fact: The top of the Shwedagon is set with thousands of diamonds and rubies.

name: Guatapé Rock (El Peñol), Colombia
clues: A giant gray rock with a zigzag of stairs, / above blue lakes and islands, it's worth all the prayers.
I'm a huge granite rock with 740 steps above a reservoir near Medellín, Colombia. What am I?
A giant rock with a zigzag staircase near Medellín, Colombia.
fact: About 740 steps lead to the top of El Peñol.

name: Hallstatt, Austria
clues: Pastel houses squeezed between a lake and a peak, / so pretty that China built a copy, a replica sleek.
I'm a lakeside village in the Salzkammergut region of Austria. What am I?
A lakeside village in the Austrian Alps.
fact: Hallstatt's bone house holds hundreds of painted skulls, because the tiny graveyard ran out of space.

name: Ha Long Bay, Vietnam
clues: Two thousand green islands rise out of the sea, / where junk boats with red sails float lazy and free.
My name means descending dragon, and I'm a bay of limestone islands in northern Vietnam. What am I?
A bay of green islands in northern Vietnam.
fact: Ha Long means 'descending dragon' in Vietnamese.

name: Belém Tower, Lisbon, Portugal
clues: A white stone tower that stood in the river, / where caravels left, to the world they'd deliver.
I'm a riverside fortress at the mouth of the Tagus, in Lisbon, Portugal. What am I?
A riverside fortress at the mouth of the Tagus in Lisbon.
fact: The rhino carving is thought to show the rhinoceros sent to Lisbon from India in 1515.

name: Hagia Sophia, Istanbul, Türkiye
clues: A great floating dome with four minarets tall, / it's been a church and a mosque, through it all.
I'm the great domed building of old Constantinople, in Istanbul, Türkiye. What am I?
The great domed building of old Constantinople.
fact: Hagia Sophia's main dome rises about 55 m above the floor.

name: Persepolis, Iran
clues: Stone columns and stairs where the Persian kings stood, / with carvings of nations bringing gifts as they should.
I'm the ruins of the ancient Persian capital, near Shiraz in southern Iran. What am I?
The ceremonial capital of the ancient Persian Empire.
fact: Persepolis was founded by Darius the Great around 518 BC.

name: Oia, Santorini, Greece
clues: White houses and blue domes on a volcano's rim, / where crowds clap the sunset as the light grows dim.
I'm a clifftop village on Santorini, in Greece's Aegean islands. What am I?
White houses and blue domes on a Greek island in the Aegean.
fact: The Minoan eruption of Santorini was one of the largest volcanic eruptions in human history.

name: Ephesus, Türkiye
clues: A two-story library facade made of stone, / and a theater for thousands, in ruins, alone.
I'm the ruins of a great ancient city with the Library of Celsus, near Türkiye's Aegean coast. What am I?
An ancient Greek and Roman city near Selçuk, on Türkiye's Aegean coast.
fact: The Library of Celsus at Ephesus once held about 12,000 scrolls.

name: Göreme, Cappadocia, Türkiye
clues: Rock chimneys and cave homes and balloons at dawn, / hundreds float up, before the sun's fully on.
I'm a valley of fairy chimneys and cave churches in Cappadocia, central Türkiye. What am I?
The land of fairy chimneys in central Türkiye.
fact: Derinkuyu, an underground city nearby, goes down about 85 m and could shelter thousands.

name: Hobbiton, Matamata, New Zealand
clues: Round doors in green hills and a pub by a lake, / no hobbit lives here, but the tourists still make.
I'm a movie village of hobbit holes on a sheep farm on New Zealand's North Island. What am I?
The hobbit village film set on New Zealand's North Island.
fact: Hobbiton was rebuilt in permanent materials for The Hobbit films and is now a tourist attraction.

name: Sidi Bou Said, Tunisia
clues: A village of white with doors painted blue, / on a cliff over the sea, with a sweet mint tea view.
I'm a blue-and-white clifftop village just outside Tunis, Tunisia. What am I?
A blue-and-white clifftop village near Tunis, Tunisia.
fact: A 1915 rule says the village's houses must stay white with blue doors and shutters.

name: Boudhanath Stupa, Kathmandu, Nepal
clues: A white dome with eyes that look out every way, / where prayer flags flutter and pilgrims walk all day.
I'm one of the biggest stupas in the world, in Kathmandu, Nepal. What am I?
The giant white stupa with painted eyes in Kathmandu, Nepal.
fact: Boudhanath is one of the largest stupas in the world, and pilgrims walk around it clockwise.

name: Timbuktu, Mali
clues: Mosques made of mud at the edge of the sand, / where salt and gold traded, and books filled the land.
I'm a legendary desert city near the Niger River in Mali, whose name means the middle of nowhere. What am I?
A legendary desert city in Mali whose name starts with 'Tim'.
fact: Timbuktu's Djinguereber Mosque was built around 1327 and is still made of mud brick.

name: Monaco
clues: A rock full of yachts and a palace by the sea, / where race cars roar through a tunnel, past me.
I'm a tiny country on the French Riviera, famous for its casino and Grand Prix. What am I?
A tiny principality on the French Riviera.
fact: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world after Vatican City.

name: Fushimi Inari Shrine, Kyoto, Japan
clues: Ten thousand orange gates in a tunnel uphill, / with stone foxes guarding, so quiet and still.
I'm a mountain shrine of thousands of orange torii gates, in Kyoto, Japan. What am I?
Fushimi Inari shrine in Kyoto.
fact: The paths of torii gates at Fushimi Inari wind about 4 km up Mount Inari.

name: Jemaa el-Fnaa, Marrakech, Morocco
clues: Snake charmers and juice stands and smoke from the grill, / a square that comes alive when the night air is still.
I'm the great market square of Marrakech, in the shadow of the Koutoubia minaret, Morocco. What am I?
The great square of Morocco's Red City.
fact: The square was one of the first places on UNESCO's list of Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2001.

name: Panama Canal, Panama
clues: Ships climb up water stairs, ocean to ocean, / through locks and a lake, in a slow, steady motion.
I'm the canal across the narrowest part of Central America, linking two oceans. What am I?
The canal across a narrow Central American country.
fact: Each ship passing through the Panama Canal uses about 200 million liters of fresh water from Gatun Lake.

name: Gergeti Trinity Church, Georgia
clues: A little stone church on a green hill alone, / below a white peak, where the clouds make their home.
I'm a hilltop church under Mount Kazbek, in the Caucasus Mountains of Georgia. What am I?
A hilltop church below Mount Kazbek, in the Caucasus of Georgia.
fact: The church stands at about 2,170 m, under the 5,054 m summit of Mount Kazbek.

name: Half Dome, Yosemite, USA
clues: A granite dome sliced down its face like bread, / climbers pull up on cables to reach its head.
I'm a giant granite dome in Yosemite Valley, California. What am I?
A granite dome in Yosemite National Park, California.
fact: Half Dome rises about 1,444 m above the floor of Yosemite Valley.

name: Lake Bled, Slovenia
clues: A church on an island in a green alpine lake, / with a castle on a cliff, and a cream cake to take.
I'm an alpine lake with a church on an island, in the Julian Alps of Slovenia. What am I?
An alpine lake with a church on an island, in Slovenia.
fact: Bled's island is the only natural island in Slovenia.

name: Sigiriya, Sri Lanka
clues: A palace on a rock rising out of the trees, / you climb through two lion paws, if you please.
I'm the Lion Rock fortress in the middle of Sri Lanka. What am I?
The Lion Rock fortress in Sri Lanka.
fact: Sigiriya was built by King Kashyapa in the 5th century.

name: Marina Bay Sands, Singapore
clues: Three towers that carry a ship on their heads, / with a pool at the edge, where the skyline spreads.
I'm a hotel with a rooftop infinity pool, beside the Gardens by the Bay, in Singapore. What am I?
A famous hotel on the waterfront of a city-state.
fact: Singapore is one of only three surviving city-states.

name: Tulum, Mexico
clues: Maya ruins on a cliff by the turquoise sea, / where iguanas sunbathe on old stones by me.
I'm a Maya city on a cliff over the Caribbean, south of Cancún, Mexico. What am I?
Maya ruins on a cliff over the Caribbean, in Mexico's Yucatán.
fact: Tulum was one of the last cities the Maya built, and people still lived there when the Spanish arrived.

name: Maya Bay, Thailand
clues: A beach in a cove that's walled in by stone, / so famous from a movie, it needed time alone.
I'm a cove on the Phi Phi Islands, in the Andaman Sea off southern Thailand. What am I?
A cove on Ko Phi Phi Le in the Andaman Sea.
fact: Maya Bay was closed from 2018 to 2022 to let its coral and sharks recover.

name: Waitomo Glowworm Caves, New Zealand
clues: A dark river cave where a galaxy glows, / not stars, but tiny worms, as the boat slowly goes.
I'm a cave lit by thousands of glowworms, on New Zealand's North Island. What am I?
Caves lit by glowworms on New Zealand's North Island.
fact: The glowworms are actually the larvae of a small fly.

name: Sundarbans, Bangladesh
clues: A forest of mangroves where tigers can swim, / in a delta of rivers, so muddy and dim.
I'm the world's biggest mangrove forest, in the Ganges delta, in Bangladesh. What am I?
The mangrove forest of the Ganges delta in Bangladesh, home of Bengal tigers.
fact: The Sundarbans is the largest mangrove forest in the world, shared by Bangladesh and India.

name: The Bund, Shanghai, China
clues: Old banks in a row by a river so wide, / face a skyline of futuristic towers on the other side.
I'm the colonial waterfront of Shanghai, China, facing Pudong. What am I?
Shanghai's famous waterfront.
fact: The Shanghai Tower across the river is the tallest building in China.

name: Potala Palace, Lhasa, Tibet
clues: A red-and-white palace that climbs up a hill, / on the roof of the world, standing proud and still.
I'm the palace of the Dalai Lamas in Lhasa, Tibet. What am I?
A red-and-white palace in Lhasa.
fact: The Potala Palace is 13 stories tall and was built in the 1600s on an older site.

name: Abu Simbel, Egypt
clues: Four giant kings carved in rock by the Nile, / they were moved up a hill, to stay dry for a while.
I'm a temple of four giant statues of Ramesses II, in the far south of Egypt near Sudan. What am I?
Giant statues of Ramesses II near the Sudan border.
fact: Moving Abu Simbel took four years and a global campaign led by UNESCO.

name: Bondi Beach, Sydney, Australia
clues: Golden sand, surfers and a pool by the sea, / where waves crash right in, and swimmers swim free.
I'm Sydney's most famous surf beach, in Australia. What am I?
Sydney's famous surf beach.
fact: The Bondi Icebergs pool, cut into the rocks at the south end, opened in 1929.
